absent: Decompressor selection macro, page-extension routine, mapping flags and page protections beyond call sites.
Global duplicate-request list, duplicate-trace flag, waiter sleep state and workqueue identity beyond uses shown.
Module subsystem object lifecycle, attribute teardown, and livepatch flag semantics beyond setters shown.
Architecture-specific section prepend overrides and function-descriptor dereference overrides beyond weak defaults.
Signature checking, version checking, tree insertion semantics, parameter locking and ELF copy behavior when enabled.
Statistics counters, failed-module list handling, and unloaded-tainted-module reporting beyond inline fallbacks.

findings.text: Module image decompression prepares paged scratch storage sized from the compressed length, runs the configured decompression routine into those pages, then maps the pages into a contiguous header and records the resulting length. Its cleanup counterpart releases any mapping, frees each used page, frees the page pointer array, and resets paging state. A disabled-feature variant reports lack of support and does nothing on cleanup.

Kernel exposes a read-only module attribute reporting the build-time compression method name with a trailing newline. Initialization registers this attribute under the module subsystem object, warns on registration failure, and still reports overall success.

Duplicate load tracking uses a heap object holding a reference count, a global list linkage, a fixed-length module name buffer, a completion event signalling first-request finish, a delayed work item for deferred reclamation, and an integer slot preserving the first result for waiters.

A dedicated mutex serializes the global duplicate-request list. Lookup asserts the mutex is held. Existence checks, result announcement, and deferred list unlinking each hold it only for short list access and reference handling, while blocking wait for first-request completion happens after releasing it.

First blocking request for an unseen name creates and links a tracker and proceeds as leader; first nonblocking request bypasses tracking and proceeds untracked. A later duplicate emits a warning or trace, then either returns immediately with success when nonblocking or waits in a killable state and inherits the leader result when blocking. Announcement stores the leader outcome, wakes all waiters exactly once, and queues timed removal about a minute later.

Transient module loading state aggregates the requested name, temporary module pointer, header pointer and length, section header and string resources, symbol and string offsets, signature status, optional paging state for decompression, and an index table locating symbol, string, module, version, info, per-CPU and extended-version sections.

Exported symbol description has two build-dependent layouts, one using value and pointer fields and another using offset fields, each carrying value, name and namespace information. Symbol lookup arguments bundle requested name plus license and warning inputs with owner, checksum, symbol and license outputs. Module reference linkage pairs source and target module pointers with two list nodes.

Failure and taint accounting objects hold a list linkage, a fixed-length name, and counters or masks for load failures and taints. Address-range tracking holds minimum and maximum bounds for module text and optionally data, with optional latch-tree root when tree lookup is enabled. Extended version iteration state holds remaining count plus checksum and name cursors.

Section spare size field multiplexes allocation-region type in its high bits and byte offset in its low bits. Width, shift and masks derive from machine word size. Offset computation adds an architecture prepend size, aligns by section requirement, advances region size, and packs type with offset while asserting no overlap between offset and type bits. Core-symbol filtering decodes the type to exclude init regions.

Stable constants include a zero small-section flag, a four-bit entity-type width, a 256-character module path limit, a module-flags buffer size derived from taint count plus overhead, a module parameter prefix string, and a module log prefix string.

Symbol table layout reserves init-region room for complete symbol and string sections plus per-symbol type bytes and temporary metadata, and core-region room for a filtered symbol subset, compacted strings and matching type bytes, recording offsets for each area. Population classifies every symbol, copies the retained subset with rebased string offsets into core storage, points init metadata at the full tables, publishes it, and records the retained count.

Symbol classification derives a single-letter type from binding, section index, section flags and type, and section-name prefix, with distinct handling for weak, undefined, absolute, per-CPU, executable, read-only, writable, small-data, uninitialized and debug symbols. Core retention always keeps the first entry, keeps everything for livepatch modules, and otherwise keeps named symbols in valid allocated non-init sections with additional executable and per-CPU conditions.

Decompression mapping or size failures trigger full cleanup with propagated error. Duplicate tracker lifetime relies on reference counting with automatic free, plus delayed work that unlinks under lock and drops a reference; announcement ignores missing or already completed trackers. Killable duplicate wait propagates interruption to the duplicate caller instead of inheriting the leader result.

When optional features are disabled the lane provides inert fallbacks: decompression reports not supported, duplicate wait reports no duplicate and announcement does nothing, module tree, signature, version, sysfs, kallsyms, ELF copy and taint helpers return success or do nothing, and modinfo iteration plus empty-section testing retain their small enabled logic.

Function descriptor dereference and architecture section prepend are weak defaults returning the input pointer unchanged and zero respectively. Build identifier initialization scans non-empty note sections and records the first successfully parsed identifier, with an empty fallback when the feature is unavailable.
